//: The interactive half. Builds the repo's one ../Dockerfile, same as docker/compose.yaml, so the two front ends cannot drift into different toolchains. HOST_UID/HOST_GID default to 1000 here because devcontainer.json cannot run `id -u`; on a host where you are not uid 1000, either edit these two values or use devtools/devcontainer.sh, which passes the real ones.
name: rustflow
//mounts: Every entry matches docker/compose.yaml's `dev` service, so the two front ends share one cargo registry and one /target instead of a cold copy each, and agree on where Claude Code's config comes from. (1,2) the build caches. (3) the host's ~/.claude, bound READ-WRITE at $HOME/.claude (HOME is pinned in the Dockerfile so this path can be named here): the container is logged in because you are. A directory and not just the credentials file inside it, because a single-file bind mount cannot be replaced by rename -- see the long comment in compose.yaml. (4,5) shadow two subtrees back out of that bind so the container cannot write host plugin state. (6) ~/.claude.json, READ-ONLY and under a different name, for postCreateCommand to copy: it sits beside the config dir rather than in it, and is one monolithic JSON rewritten whole on each change, so it is copied rather than shared. NOTE: unlike devtools/devcontainer.sh, which creates or tests for a source first, this file cannot -- so on a host that has never run Claude Code, drop entries 3 and 6.
//containerEnv: All three are optional and forwarded from the host, matching the `environment:` list in docker/compose.yaml. ${localEnv:VAR} expands to the empty string when the host has no such variable, and an empty value is not a configured credential. Claude Code's two are usually not wanted at all here -- the ~/.claude mount above already logs the container in -- and exist for a host that has no ~/.claude to mount. GH_TOKEN is not optional in the same way: it is the only thing that authenticates gh, and the only way git push works.
//postCreateCommand: The same script devtools/devcontainer.sh runs after its own `up`, so the two front ends cannot drift: it sets up git push credentials from GH_TOKEN and seeds Claude Code's config from the mount above. Per-created-container, which is right -- both of those land in the container's own filesystem.
